business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Ashutosh Fibre Limited manufactures technical and synthetic yarns and fabrics at its facility in Petlad, Gujarat, using Ring Spun, DREF (Friction Spun) and Open-End spinning technologies across five processing lines, supported by two-for-one twisting and splicing. It operates a business-to-business model, supplying industrial manufacturers, processors and institutional buyers who use the yarns as raw-material inputs in filtration and pollution control, construction and infrastructure, automotive friction materials, packaging, protective equipment and home furnishing. Alongside its own product range it undertakes job work on customer-supplied raw material and trades in yarn, with manufacturing the principal activity.

cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: Backward integration is centred on in-house fibre regeneration rather than upstream fibre manufacture. The Company imports end-of-life para-aramid fabrics (e.g. expired bulletproof vests) and runs a dedicated regenerating machine for high-strength fibres supporting a proprietary 'Fabric-to-Fibre' recycling process that breaks down and reconstitutes aramid fabrics while retaining tensile strength and thermal resistance; the recycled fibres are fed back as secondary raw material into brake pads, clutch facings, filtration media and protective textiles, reducing dependence on imported virgin fibres and lowering raw material cost. Beyond this, the Company is a single-stage spinner: raw fibre is bought in (polypropylene fibre, high-tenacity polyester, modacrylic fibre, para-aramid fibre, FR viscose fibre and specialised blends such as melamine and peroxidised PAN) and converted through blowroom, carding, drawing, roving, ring frame / DREF friction spinning / open-end spinning, winding, TFO doubling, rewinding and packing, all at the single Petlad unit. Procurement is managed by a Purchase and Supply Chain Department across a mixed domestic and international vendor base with no long-term supply agreements; specialty fibres are largely imported (imports 36.92% of total purchase in FY25) while polypropylene and polyester are domestic. Forward integration is limited - the Company sells B2B into converters and does not process into finished fabrics or garments, though it operates a fabric line within Protech and takes job work where customers supply the raw material (Rs 1,009.09 lakhs, 8.85% of FY25 revenue from operations) and does a small amount of yarn trading (Rs 305.28 lakhs, 2.68%). Energy is partially self-supplied: a 380 KW rooftop solar system at Petlad plus a 4 MW captive solar plant on leased land at Kankanpur, expected to substitute a significant portion of electricity requirements from FY 2025-26. Utilities are otherwise bought in (power from Madhya Gujarat Vij Company Ltd, industrial water by tanker from a local supplier). Manpower as of August 31, 2025 is approximately 156 permanent employees (2 executive directors, 8 finance/accounts/administration, 1 legal and secretarial, 5 technical staff, 2 quality management, 6 sales and marketing, 14 supervisors and in-charges, 118 skilled and unskilled staff), with 119 registered under EPF and no contract labour employed.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Raw material availability and cost — manufacturing depends on third-party supply of polypropylene fibre, high-tenacity polyester, modacrylic, para-aramid, FR viscose, melamine and peroxidised PAN, with no long-term supply agreements; shortages or price swings flow straight into cost structure
- Customer concentration — a significant portion of revenue comes from key customers; top 1 / 3 / 5 / 10 customers were 19.75% / 39.77% / 51.57% / 67.40% of revenue from operations in Fiscal 2025
- Supplier concentration — top 1 / 3 / 5 / 10 suppliers were 13.19% / 35.71% / 52.26% / 70.31% of total purchases in Fiscal 2025
- Product-mix shift within the yarn portfolio — para-aramid based spun yarn fell from 32.10% of revenue in Fiscal 2024 to 23.87% in Fiscal 2025 while meta aramid / viscose / para aramid based spun yarn rose from 3.69% to 12.64%
- Export exposure and foreign trade policy — exports were ₹ 4,339.15 lakhs (38.05%), ₹ 4,789.49 lakhs (43.59%) and ₹ 3,539.55 lakhs (36.15%) of revenue in Fiscals 2025, 2024 and 2023, with export obligations under duty exemption schemes
- Working capital build — trade receivables rose 25.26% to ₹ 1,928.12 lakhs and inventories 13.63% to ₹ 1,443.08 lakhs in Fiscal 2025, against trade payables of ₹ 449.71 lakhs
- Leverage and interest cost — long-term borrowings rose 120.11% to ₹ 3,090.25 lakhs in Fiscal 2025 on secured borrowings from Citi Bank N.A., and short-term borrowings rose 27.42% to ₹ 2,653.25 lakhs largely on director loans (₹ 808.22 lakhs to ₹ 1,289.30 lakhs); debt-equity ratio moved from 1.27x to 1.60x
- Capital intensity — the business requires continued investment in manufacturing technologies and running capital-intensive production facilities at optimal efficiency
- Quality yield and rejection control — minimising defects and rejections is stated to improve customer satisfaction and operating margins
- Captive solar substitution of grid power expected to reduce electricity expense from Fiscal 2025-26 onwards
- Retention of skilled personnel across specialised manufacturing processes; workforce of 131 permanent employees as of March 31, 2025, with employee benefit expense at 4.93% of revenue from operations in Fiscal 2025

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Production capacity enhancement and cost optimisation by expanding within the existing Petlad facility, deploying additional compact spinning systems and high-value yarn attachments such as the Pinter Hard Core system for core-spun and specialty yarns, while leveraging shared infrastructure, workforce and administrative functions to optimise capital expenditure
- Expand global market reach — invest in capital expenditure to increase installed capacity, scale volumes to service international markets and gradually grow the proportion of revenue generated from exports, targeting additional export markets for specialised technical yarns
- Expansion into higher-value technical textile markets, entering milled acrylic and milled carbon yarns for fire-resistant fabrics, composite reinforcement and advanced industrial textiles
- Automation and digitisation across manufacturing and administrative processes — integrated planning systems, automated inventory management and data-driven monitoring and analytics
- Enhance capacity and capabilities in the Indutech and Protech segments where demand for high-performance, application-specific textile materials is growing across chemicals, pharmaceuticals, safety equipment and industrial filtration
- Renewable energy and sustainability — captive solar generation to reduce electricity cost and carbon footprint, and circular-economy fibre recycling

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The expansion is a brownfield capacity build inside the existing leased Petlad, Gujarat plant (Building Nos. 27, 28 and 29, City Survey No. 156, Station Road, Village Petlad, Ahmedabad – 388450), which spans approximately 53,988.88 sq. m of which only about 20,570.89 sq. m is currently utilised, leaving room to expand without new land. ₹ 2,495.75 lakhs of Net Proceeds is earmarked for purchase and installation of additional equipment and machinery — including civil/factory-building work of ₹ 459.89 lakhs and machinery such as Savio Proxima I Smartconer automatic cone winders, SMEW Filcono assembly winding machines and LMW blowroom, carding and draw-frame lines — deployed ₹ 1,247.87 lakhs in Fiscal 2026 and ₹ 1,247.88 lakhs in Fiscal 2027. The stated rationale is that existing utilisation is already high (86.58% on the 3,750 MT synthetic-yarn line in Fiscal 2025) and that against an estimated demand of 120 MT the Company is currently able to manufacture only 55 MT, meeting approximately 44% of demand. The new machinery is intended to substantially increase capacity, improve operational efficiency and broaden the range into para-aramid, flame-retardant, high-tenacity polyester and nylon, speciality blended and other technical yarns for gloves, conveyor belts, tarpaulins and coated fabrics, supporting the strategy of expanding within the existing industrial framework and growing exports. Separately, the Company has commissioned a 380 KW rooftop solar system at Petlad and a 4 MW captive solar plant on leased land at Village Kankanpur, Taluka Godhra, District Panchmahal, expected to substitute a significant portion of electricity requirements from Fiscal 2025-26.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Proprietary “Fabric-to-Fibre” recycling of end-of-life para-aramid fabrics using a dedicated regenerating machine for high-strength fibres, converting imported expired material into secondary raw material for brake pads, clutch facings, filtration media and protective textiles — lowering dependence on imported virgin fibre and raw-material cost
- Established position in polypropylene spun yarns, which accounted for approximately 22.64%, 21.27% and 26.66% of revenue from operations in Fiscals 2025, 2024 and 2023
- Diversified manufacturing base of five processing lines and three spinning technologies (Ring Spun, DREF friction spun and Open-End) spanning counts from 0.4 Ne to 50 Ne with up to six plies, allowing customisation to client specifications
- Long-standing customer and supplier relationships producing a high proportion of repeat business; a significant portion of raw material is met through the top 5 suppliers
- Quality control infrastructure including electronic yarn clearing systems, Mesdan Evenness Tester and Pinter Hard Core attachment; defect and rejection rates of 0.40%, 0.03% and 0.13% of revenue from operations in Fiscals 2025, 2024 and 2023
- ESG alignment via a commissioned 380 KW rooftop solar system and a 4 MW captive solar plant, plus ISO 9001/14001/45001, 5S and OEKO-TEX Standard 100 certifications valued by global customers

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Single-facility, single-segment concentration — All manufacturing is carried out at one facility at Petlad, Gujarat, and the Company operates in a single business segment — spinning of technical textile yarn. Any disruption, slowdown or shutdown at Petlad, or adverse developments in that one segment, hits the entire business with no alternative site or offsetting vertical.
- Customer concentration — Top 1 / 3 / 5 / 10 customers contributed 19.75% / 39.77% / 51.57% / 67.40% of revenue from operations in Fiscal 2025 (25.53% / 47.85% / 57.91% / 72.11% in Fiscal 2024). Loss of one large customer, a decline in its financial health or reduced demand would materially affect revenue and cash flow. China alone accounted for 19.75% of Fiscal 2025 revenue, matching the top-1 customer figure.
- Raw material dependence without long-term supply agreements — There are no long-term agreements for supply of raw materials, and the majority is sourced from the top 10 suppliers (70.31% of purchases in Fiscal 2025). Para-aramid, viscose and acrylic fibres come from a limited number of customer-approved suppliers, so substitution is slow and disruption or price escalation passes into production schedules, volumes and margins.
- Product concentration in two yarn families — The business is heavily dependent on para-aramid based spun yarn and 100% polypropylene spun yarn, disclosed at 23.87% and 22.64% of revenue from operations respectively in Fiscal 2025 (32.10% and 21.27% in Fiscal 2024). Any fall in demand, inability to produce, or adverse price movement in these two yarns disproportionately affects results.
- Everything material operates on leased premises — The registered office, the Petlad manufacturing unit, the rooftop solar facility and the 4 MW ground-mounted solar project are all on leased property, and the Issue proceeds will install machinery on a leased factory. Early termination, non-renewal, or renewal on worse terms would jeopardise both operations and the return on Issue-funded capex.
- Export obligations under duty exemption schemes and foreign-trade-policy exposure — Exports were 38.05% of Fiscal 2025 revenue from operations and the Company carries an obligation to export against import of ₹ 535.82 lakhs as at March 31, 2025 (₹ 343.53 lakhs in Fiscal 2024). Failure to meet export obligations, or adverse changes in foreign trade policy or tariffs, would trigger duty liabilities and hurt cash flows.
- Leverage, negative cash flows and reliance on promoter/director funding — Debt-equity ratio rose to 1.60x in Fiscal 2025 from 1.27x, long-term borrowings grew 120.11% to ₹ 3,090.25 lakhs and short-term borrowings included director loans of ₹ 1,289.30 lakhs; short loans received from related parties were ₹ 1,778.63 lakhs in Fiscal 2025. The Company has also experienced negative cash flows in the recent past. ₹ 2,500.00 lakhs of Net Proceeds is earmarked to repay borrowings, so post-Issue re-leveraging is the item to watch.
- Capital intensity and execution of the Issue-funded expansion — The proposed expansion depends on purchasing and installing new equipment and machinery for ₹ 2,495.75 lakhs against quotations, not firm orders, deployed across Fiscals 2026 and 2027. If investment in manufacturing technology falls short, or the added capacity is not absorbed at the assumed demand (an estimated 120 MT against present 55 MT capability), competitiveness and returns suffer.

commitments.title: Promises (RHP)
commitments.body:
- **Deploy ₹ 2,495.75 lakhs of Net Proceeds towards new equipment and machinery at the existing Petlad manufacturing facility, split ₹ 1,247.87 lakhs in Fiscal 2026 and ₹ 1,247.88 lakhs in Fiscal 2027.**
- **Repay or pre-pay, in full or in part, ₹ 2,500.00 lakhs of certain borrowings availed by the Company, entirely from Net Proceeds in Fiscal 2026.**
- **General corporate purposes will be capped at the lower of 15% of gross proceeds or ₹ 1,000.00 lakhs.**
- **Scale up production capacity by expanding operations within the existing Petlad facility, deploying additional compact spinning systems and high-value yarn attachments such as the Pinter Hard Core system for core-spun and specialty yarns.**
- **Expand manufacturing to close the stated gap between an estimated demand of 120 MT and current manufacturing ability of 55 MT, which meets approximately 44% of demand.**
- **Expand global market reach and gradually grow the proportion of revenue generated from exports by adding capacity and targeting additional export markets for specialised technical yarns.**
- **Diversify the product portfolio by entering high-value technical yarn markets such as milled acrylic and milled carbon yarns for fire-resistant fabrics, composite reinforcement and advanced industrial textiles.**
- **Enhance capacity and capabilities in the Indutech and Protech segments, where demand for high-performance and application-specific textile materials is growing across chemicals, pharmaceuticals, safety equipment manufacturing and …**
- **Expand adoption of automation and digital tools across manufacturing and administrative processes, including integrated planning systems, automated inventory management and data-driven monitoring and analytics.**
- **The commissioned 4 MW captive solar power plant is expected to substitute a significant portion of the Company's electricity requirements from Financial Year 2025-26 onwards, contributing to cost savings.**
- **Outstanding obligation to export against import under duty exemption schemes stood at ₹ 535.82 lakhs as at March 31, 2025, up from ₹ 343.53 lakhs a year earlier; non-compliance would trigger duty liabilities.**
- **The Company, in consultation with the BRLM, may undertake a Pre-IPO Placement not exceeding 20% of the size of the Issue, with any amount so raised reduced from the Issue.**
